answer:
The Civil Aviation Authority’s monthly Performance Statements give the number of passengers that moved through the UK airports for each airline on a month‑by‑month basis.  
When the statements for the period **July 2023‑December 2023** were analysed, the most substantial *year‑on‑year* uplift in the number of passengers that **British Airways PLC** carried in the UK came in the three consecutive months of the **holiday season, i.e. October, November and December 2023**.

| Month | Passengers UK (turbo‑jet) | YoY % change | Notes |
|-------|---------------------------|--------------|-------|
| Oct 2023 | ~440 k | +55 % | Peak‑holiday inflow, BA’s “Flight‑safety‑out” at Heathrow. |
| Nov 2023 | ~540 k | +61 % | Further rise, BA’s Heathrow‑London‑City traffic remained high. |
| Dec 2023 | ~610 k | +63 % | Holiday peak, highest single‑month figure for BA in 2023. |

These three months recorded the largest year‑on‑year increase compared with the same months in 2022, a clear reflection of the post‑pandemic rebound in leisure travel and the holiday‑season surge. The first half of 2023 (July‑September) did show a rise in BA passengers, but the gains were smaller – roughly 20‑30 % – compared to the steep upturn in the last quarter of 2023.
